analysis:
Unit 0829a6ebd1708351:5 is the head-side text of GLM5NextPromptPolicyTests.swift (lines 509-850), a test-only file. It adds or updates tests for: OpenRouter reasoning-content return shapes; the `thinking` object and its `clear_thinking` precedence; empty tool-call arguments rendering as `{}`; exact large-integer schema handling (an overflow integer is rejected before rounding); and internal marker handling. A forged `x-darkbloom-original-boolean-schema` marker is rejected only when the actual model type is glm5_next, and a caller-supplied model_type is not treated as authority. The tests check that tool-call/tool-result IDs match exactly, that malformed arguments are rejected, and that non-GLM families keep their legacy behavior.

I found no production code changes in this unit, so no control is weakened and there is no new attack surface. Any security effect depends on the production prompt-normalization code (the ProviderPromptContractPipeline, GLM5NextPromptPolicy.RawControls and ProviderLoop.decodeOpenAIRequest sources), which was not supplied in this unit. The tests suggest broader acceptance of OpenRouter reasoning fields, but they only constrain prompt rendering. They do not touch the threat model's assets: attestation, key custody, the prefix cache, or the coordinator/provider WebSocket leg. A-001 (consumer prompts) is the only plausibly related asset, and the tests show no plaintext exposure or logging. The patch excerpt was truncated and the base side was not supplied, so I could not compare against the original assertions. The next pass should check that the production decoders implement the strictness these tests assert, in particular that the marker rejection applies only to the actual model identity and that duplicate keys and out-of-range numbers are rejected.
